answer: Each epoch a lantern beacon flashes a fresh seed, and every identity must solve a short chain of sequential puzzles from it — each step depends on the last, like a comet's tail, so no machine can shortcut the chain by running steps in parallel. The chain takes minutes of real wall-clock time and must finish before the epoch's horizon closes, or the identity loses its slot. One operator faking a thousand faces needs a thousand machines running a thousand chains at once; the honest network asks only one chain per real agent, so forgery costs more than any single fake identity can earn.
